newsitem.title: USA: Hayes to use Alcatel ADSL modem chips.
newsitem.headline: Hayes to use Alcatel ADSL modem chips.

text.p: Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc. said its high-speed modem deal with Alcatel Alsthom, which was announced Monday, calls for Hayes to use underlying semiconductor technology developed by Alcatel's Mietec unit.

Atlanta-based Hayes plans to use Mietec chipsets in the Asymmetrical Digital Subscriber Line modem products Hayes is building to work with the complete ADSL system Alcatel is developing for installation by large telephone companies.
Hayes plan to use Mietec chipset in all its Alcatel ADSL products. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
However, the deal is not exclusive and Hayes is free to use other suppliers' semiconductor technology in other ADSL products it may develop, spokesmen for the two companies said.
In January, Hayes had announced a licensing deal to use ADSL software from Aware Inc and semiconductor chipsets built by Analog Devices Inc.
Alcatel is based in Paris. The ADSL development work takes place at engineering centers in Antwerp, Belgium and Raleigh, N.C. Alcatel's Mietec unit is based in Brussels.
